title: Self-Enhanced Density Clustering for High Dimension and Low Sample Size Data

problem.claim: Clustering high-dimensional and low sample size data is challenged by extreme sparsity and noise, while spectral methods suffer from degraded distance metrics and deep clustering tends to over-fit scarce data.

contributions.claim: A Self-Enhanced Density Clustering framework integrates cluster structure discovery and embedding representation learning through an iterative enhancement process.
The framework uses adaptive density-derived centroids to parameterize probabilistic soft labels that supervise a lightweight multilayer perceptron for low-dimensional embedding learning.
The learned embedding is used to refine the metric space and generate improved labels in subsequent interaction steps through mutual reinforcement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 43 challenging HDLSS datasets reportedly demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and substantially outperform popular clustering methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: HDLSS clustering is difficult because sparsity and noise confound cluster analysis.
Spectral methods fail as distances degrade, while deep clustering can over-fit scarce data.
SEDC combines cluster discovery and embedding learning in an iterative enhancement process.
The embedding refines the metric space, and feedback between embedding discrimination and labels progressively reinforces the process while mitigating over-fitting.
The authors report strong results across 43 HDLSS datasets and describe the approach as a promising solution for robust HDLSS clustering.

source_observation.claim: Iteratively coupling representation learning with cluster-label refinement is reported to improve the embedding metric space and subsequent labels.

interpretation.claim: Mutual reinforcement between representations and labels may help clustering when the original distance structure is unreliable.

application.claim: For HDLSS clustering, consider lightweight representation learning supervised by adaptive density-derived soft labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond HDLSS settings or which data conditions limit its effectiveness.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the 43 datasets.
Evaluation metrics, baseline methods, and numerical performance results are not specified.
Implementation details and the basis for the reported state-of-the-art comparison are not provided.
